A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main texts, equations, eight figures, thirteen tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite repagination.

before.justification: V1 reports original clustering and image-decomposition experiments, component ablations, timing measurements, and appendix hyperparameter-sensitivity results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 2–9, Figure 7, and appendix Table 13.

M1.justification: The sprite-generation, transformation, selection, composition, and regularization procedures remain unchanged. Sections 3–5 and Table 1 specify the same clustering and decomposition models.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight clustering datasets and Tetrominoes, Multi-dSprites, CLEVR6, and CLEVR. No training or evaluation domain or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the experiments, including DTI-Clustering in Table 7 and DTI-Sprites, MarioNette, and AST-Seg-B3-CT in their corresponding decomposition comparisons.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, training budgets, model configurations, transformations, and hyperparameter-search ranges remain unchanged. V2's additional discussion refers to existing settings documented in Tables 10–12 and Appendix .2.2.

E4.justification: The component ablations, qualitative failure examples, scaling analysis, and regularization sensitivity study are retained. The sensitivity analysis highlighted in v2 Section 4.1.2 already appeared in v1 Appendix .2.2 and Table 13.

E5.justification: The ten-run clustering and three-run decomposition reporting remain unchanged, as do standard-error versus standard-deviation conventions and Table 8's single-run flags. No new statistical estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, rankings, plotted measurements, and qualitative examples are unchanged across the result tables and figures, including Table 13. The added robustness wording reinterprets existing evidence rather than supplying new results.

T1.justification: The unified mathematical formulation, composition and regularization definitions in Equations 1–8, and linear-versus-exponential complexity reasoning are unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a unified analysis of sprite-based models and an interpretable, class-aware decomposition method that scales linearly with object count. The expanded conclusion retains these claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations asserting low hyperparameter sensitivity, linking scene complexity to stronger empty-sprite regularization, and emphasizing remaining scope for class-aware CLEVR improvement. Its conclusion repeats the label-dependent tuning limitation already disclosed in v1 Appendix .2.2.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, training schedules, search ranges, and the code link remain unchanged. Ground-truth-based tuning was already disclosed in the appendix; its repetition in the conclusion adds no concrete split or implementation specification.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work coverage are unchanged, as is the proposed method's substantive relationship to earlier clustering and sprite-based approaches.

P1.justification: V2 expands the conclusion, adds short regularization summaries in Sections 4.1.2 and 5.1.2, standardizes title and heading capitalization, and adds publication and review information. Most prose and the section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds journal headers and reflows existing material, including moving Figure 5 from page 12 to page 13. All figures and tables retain their substantive displays; no new visualization is introduced.

improvement.justification: The expanded conclusion improves accessibility and highlights an existing limitation, but v2 Section 4.1.2 introduces an unsupported assurance of low performance variance across searched hyperparameters. Unchanged Table 13 shows ColoredMNIST accuracy of 96.0% at λbin=0.001 versus 56.6% at λbin=0.01, with λfreq fixed at 0.1. This overgeneralization weakens the accuracy of the paper's interpretation, outweighing the limited presentation gains; the underlying scientific evidence is unchanged.
